title: Breaking through on Fletcher's hard keys
summary: Roy told Fletcher he could not play the hard keys but broke through at a Boston job.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Well, we'll play it back after a while and see.

Yeah, okay. See what happens. It's a funny thing about Thigpen, you know. Everybody could... You know, you get used to guys when you're working with them. Anyway, we were going to (?)... Before we get to that, we worked around.

And that was a band I went in, and... I'm telling you the truth. I went to Fletcher and told him he'd better get an older cat, man, somebody...because I couldn't make it in that band. Everything they wrote (?). They had all sharps or all the flats, and I just couldn't find them. Nowhere in my valves did they fit, you know? I couldn't find those keys no kind of way, you know. So he said, "No, you'll be all right."

And I figure when I broke through was, we played the Steiner(?) Stables in Boston, right outside of Boston. It was so funny, man, because... Well, I'm thinking about it, and next thing I know I was playing -- playing in those keys. And from then on, it was... It just like a
breakthrough. The cloud was away, you know. Of course, I spent a lot of time trying to get it together, too. And from then on I was cool, you know.
